title: LoRaWAN Payload Schema
description: Schema for defining LoRaWAN device payload codec descriptions

name.description: Field name in decoded output. Prefix with _ for internal/hidden fields.

type.description: Data type. Standard types or the bitfield range uN[start:end], e.g. u8[3:4]

consume.description: Bytes to advance after reading. 0 = don't advance (shared byte).

mult.description: Multiply raw value by this factor

div.description: Divide raw value by this factor

add.description: Add this offset to raw value

formula.description: Custom formula using 'x' for raw value and $field for cross-references

valid_range.description: Expected value bounds [min, max]. Out-of-range values produce quality warnings.

unece.description: UNECE Recommendation 20 unit code (e.g., CEL for Celsius, FAH for Fahrenheit)

var.description: Store decoded value as variable for later match/formula references

values.description: Enum values: dict {int: string} or list [string]

base.description: Base integer type for enum (default: u8)

cases.description: Match cases: legacy [{case:, fields:}] or Option B {value: [fields]}

byte_group.description:
Fields sharing one span of bytes: each is read from the same starting position and none advances it, so bit ranges over the same byte can be named separately (PS-070). The span is stepped over once, at the end.

Two spellings, both honoured everywhere. The object form carries its own `size`; the array form is the field list alone and takes `size` from the field beside it, defaulting to 1 byte. The corpus uses the object form throughout.

A member must not carry `consume` (PS-017): the construct sets it, and a member trying to advance the position would defeat the sharing.

size.description: Width of the shared span in bytes.

endian.description: The byte order the span is assembled in, its members' bit positions referring to that value (PS-364). Members declare none.

oneOf.description: The array form: the field list alone, with `size` beside it.

size.description: Width in bytes of a `byte_group` written in its array form. Ignored by the object form, which carries its own.

count.description: `type: repeat`: a fixed number of iterations, as an integer or a `$variable` naming a field already decoded. Exactly one of `count`, `byte_length` and `until` belongs on a repeat (PS-083); where more than one appears this wins, silently.

byte_length.description: `type: repeat`: iterate until this many bytes are consumed, as an integer or a `$variable`. The members must divide the span exactly; a decode that ends elsewhere is an error, not a short array (PS-088). Beaten by `count` where both appear.

until.description: `type: repeat`: iterate until the payload is exhausted. `end` is the only value (PS-086) - any other is refused rather than treated as a bound. Beaten by `count` or `byte_length` where they appear.

max.description: `type: repeat`: iteration ceiling, a guard against a malformed payload. Honoured by the four interpreters and not read by the TS013 generator, which relies on its own no-progress check instead.

min.description: `type: repeat`: fewest iterations that count as a valid decode; fewer is an error. Honoured by the four interpreters, not read by the TS013 generator.

reserve.description: `type: repeat` with `until: end`: bytes at the end of the payload the repeat must not consume; the fields after it decode from them (PS-350). An error where fewer remain at the start (PS-351).

trailer.description: `type: repeat` with `reserve`: fields decoded from the reserved bytes before the first element, bound for the elements and reported beside the repeat (PS-383). Each has a fixed size, and the sizes sum to `reserve` (PS-384). Encoded after the elements (PS-385).

index.description: `type: repeat`: a name bound to each element's zero-based position while it is decoded and encoded (PS-366, PS-370).

count_as.description: `type: repeat`: a name bound after the repeat to the number of elements it reports, after present_if (PS-367).

present_if.description: `type: repeat`: one guard condition evaluated after each element; an element for which it is false is omitted, still advancing the index (PS-386). Such a repeat cannot be encoded where its elements read bytes (PS-387).

carry.description: A computed field in a repeat's elements: its own name resolves to its value in the previous element, or to this value in the first (PS-378 to PS-381).

identity.description: `type: repeat`: its `index`, or a `$` reference to a field of its elements, identifying the metric each element carries (PS-372). An annotation; decoding ignores it (PS-376).

optional.description: Decoded where its bytes remain, absent where none do, an error where some do but too few (PS-402, PS-403). Every later field in the list must be optional too (PS-404). Encoded only where the input supplies it (PS-405).

sentinel.description: Raw integers, compared before any modifier or encoding, that mean no reading: the field is absent (PS-427, PS-429).

out_of_range.description: With valid_range: `omit` drops a value outside the range rather than reporting it flagged (PS-428).

tlv.description: TLV loop: read a tag, select the case describing it, decode that case's fields, repeat to the end of the payload (PS-153, PS-154).

tag_size.description: Width in bytes of a tag read as one integer. Mutually exclusive with tag_fields.

tag_fields.description: A composite tag, read as named fields; the tag is their values in this order. Mutually exclusive with tag_size.

tag_key.description: Names of the tag_fields that form the key, in order. Read on encode to write each component back through its own tag_fields entry. Not read by the TS013 generator, which derives the key from tag_fields directly.

length_size.description: Width in bytes of a length field following the tag. 0 or absent means the entry is undelimited, so an unrecognised tag cannot be stepped over (PS-302).

merge.description: Whether a case's fields go into the parent object (PS-156). False collects each entry into a channel list instead.

unknown.description: What to do with a tag no case describes (PS-155, PS-301 to PS-304). `skip` steps over it where a length says how long it is and otherwise abandons the rest of the payload; `raw` captures its bytes under `unknown_tags` (PS-303); `error` fails the decode. Every mode but `error` reports what it did. Implementations fall back to `skip` on an unrecognised value, so a misspelling silently discards data - tools/validate_schema.py refuses one.

reserve.description: Bytes at the end of the payload the loop must not consume; the fields after the tlv decode from them (PS-471). An error where fewer remain at the start of the tlv.

cases.description: Tag to the fields it introduces. A key is an integer (`1`, or `0x20` which YAML reads as 32); a range `"2..5"` or a list `[1, 2, 3]` for a single tag; a composite `"[1, 117]"` for a tag read through tag_fields, where a part may be `*` for any value or `!0` for any value but that one (PS-270); or `default`.

flagged.description: Bitmask-driven presence: a previously decoded field is read as a mask, and each group whose bit is set contributes its fields (PS-158). Groups are evaluated in the order written, which is the order their bytes appear (PS-160).

field.description: Name of the field holding the mask, which must already have been decoded (PS-159). A bare name - `flags`, not `$flags` - unlike the $-prefixed references used by `ref` and `compute`.

groups.description: The bits and what each introduces.

flagged_group.description: One bit of the mask and the fields its being set introduces.

bit.description: Bit position, 0 being the least significant (PS-161, PS-162). Set means this group's fields are read from the payload; clear means the group is skipped and consumes nothing. The ceiling is 63 because u64 is a flags type; the useful ceiling is the width of the referenced field. tools/validate_schema.py also refuses two groups claiming the same bit, which JSON Schema cannot express.

fields.description: Read in order where the bit is set, and merged into the parent object (PS-163). A name beginning with _ is internal: it becomes a variable later fields can reference and is not reported.

match.description:
Conditional fields chosen by a discriminator: read it, find the case that matches, decode that case's fields. The discriminator comes either from a field already decoded (`field`) or from the payload at this position (`length`).

This is the Option B spelling, the block under a `match:` key. The older spelling puts `type: match` with `on:` and a list of `{case:, fields:}` on the field itself; those keys are described on `field` rather than here.

Every key here is honoured by all five implementations. That was not true until CR-2026-020: `length` and `name` were ignored by the Go interpreter and the TS013 generator, and `var` and `default` were honoured by the Python interpreter alone, so a match reading its own discriminator decoded differently on two of the five and an unmatched value was silently skipped on four.

field.description: Name of an already-decoded field or stored variable holding the discriminator. Written with or without a leading `$`; both are accepted. Mutually exclusive with `length` in intent - where both appear this wins and `length` is ignored rather than reported.

length.description: Width in bytes of a discriminator read from the payload here, consuming those bytes. Also the width the encoder writes. Where absent and `field` is too, one byte is read.

name.description: Reports the discriminator under this key. Applies only where it was read via `length`; a discriminator taken from `field` is already in the output under its own name.

var.description: Stores the discriminator as a variable for later fields to reference, without necessarily reporting it. Applies only where it was read via `length`.

cases.description: Discriminator value to the fields it selects, the first match winning. A key is an integer (`1`, or `0x20` which YAML reads as 32); an inclusive range `"2..5"`; or `default`, which is the same as the `default` key beside it and takes precedence over it. A key that is neither an integer nor a range matches nothing on any implementation - a YAML mapping key cannot be a list, so the `[1, 2, 3]` spelling belongs to the older `case:` value form and not here.

default.description: What to do when no case matches: `error` fails the decode, `skip` leaves the remaining fields absent, or a list of fields is decoded instead. Unlike a `tlv`, whose `unknown` defaults to `skip`, this defaults to `error`.

remaining.description: Dispatch on the number of bytes from here to the end of the payload, less an enclosing repeat's reserve; reads nothing (PS-414, PS-415). Exactly one of field, length and remaining (PS-416).

payload.description: Hex string, byte array, or 0x-prefixed string

fport.description: Deprecated spelling of fPort; accepted, not emitted (PS-300)

input_metadata.description: The input context (PS-324, PS-495): TS013 input such as recvTime, and devEUI

expected_meta.description: The _meta the interpreter output must carry for this vector, compared exactly (PS-175, CR-2026-096). Absent asserts nothing.

source.description: Provenance of the expected values (PS-263). Absent means unknown, which certification treats as 'generated'.

input.description: Values to encode, for an encode vector (PS-047)

expected_payload.description: Expected encoded bytes, hex string or byte array (PS-047, PS-299)

direction.description: Direction the vector exercises; inferred from the keys when absent

port.description: Deprecated spelling of fPort; accepted, not emitted (PS-300)

expected_warnings.description: Warnings the execution must report, complete and in order (PS-305). An entry is a substring of the warning at that position, or an array of substrings all of which must appear in it (PS-306). An empty array asserts that none were reported; absent asserts nothing (PS-308).
